title: What PostgreSQL encryption at rest actually protects

images.alt: A quiet pattern of coloured sequence letters.

SQL clients receive readable rows; PostgreSQL processes them in memory, while pg_tde encrypts selected stored files. A principal key in a separate key service protects the internal keys used for those files.

title: Learning to map DNA reads by writing an aligner in Python

images.alt: Small translucent DNA letter tiles in the BioseqDB colours.
The historical mapping pipeline goes from reference chunks and shared seeds through candidate regions to endpoint refinement and coordinates.
An illustrative alignment shows a substitution, an inserted base and a deleted base in separate columns.
Overlapping three-base windows become two-bit integer keys; shifting and masking retains the latest three bases.
Three overlapping windows select three minima from the keys 6, 27, 44 and 49.
An anchor plot contrasts a long increasing path across distant regions with a compact local cluster.
Two four-anchor windows with the same query span receive different scores because the sparse window has uncovered reference gaps.
Local dynamic-programming timings compare lists and NumPy for two datasets, with the small number of calls shown.
Local endpoint-search measurements compare straightforward suffix sorting with list and NumPy variants of skew suffix-array construction.
Recorded local phase totals show where time went in the earlier prototype.
Course runtimes for ten eligible submissions across three reference sizes at approximately five percent read errors; PS is the fastest and is highlighted.
Course runtimes for the same submissions and reference sizes at approximately ten percent read errors.
PS maps all six thousand reads, with per-dataset incorrect counts of one, three, zero, zero, four and zero.
PS reported memory rises with reference size and approaches the assignment’s one-gigabyte limit.

title: Writing a small PostgreSQL table access method in C++
